title: A Regiment for the Orchard
premise: In 1911 Bristol, Edmund Hartwell drives for suffragist Adeline Voss and secretly reads the letters he carries, living vicariously through other people's history. When a census taker's probing questions expose that his papers don't match the man he claims to be, Edmund is forced into the orbit of Inspector Calloway, who suspects the Voss household of harboring fugitives. As the net tightens, Edmund discovers he has a half-sister, Nell, among the dockside families fleeing Ireland—and only one berth left on the morning ship. In the end, Edmund gives up his own name and passage to Nell, choosing found family over safety, and stays behind to testify truthfully at Adeline's trial.
about_author: Juniper Villalobos is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Edwardian census records and letters before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted orchard shed in Somerset, where she keeps the unsent correspondence that inspired this novel pinned above her desk.

chapters.title: The Man Who Delivers
chapters.summary: Edmund Hartwell, driver and self-appointed invisible man, steers Adeline Voss through Bristol while privately reading her mail. POV: Edmund. Establishes his creed—that history happens to other people—and the quiet ache beneath it.

chapters.title: Letters Not Addressed to Me
chapters.summary: Edmund reads a letter hinting someone in the Voss circle is hiding under a false name. He tells himself it's none of his business. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease as his invisibility starts to feel like complicity.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census day. The taker, Mr. Prowse, lingers over Edmund's entry and notes discrepancies in his birthplace. POV: Edmund, with a brief shift to Prowse's ledger. Beat: the floor drops—being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Orchard Behind the House
chapters.summary: Adeline tends the neglected orchard behind the house, telling Edmund about the sister she lost. He almost confesses his secret; doesn't. POV: alternating Edmund/Adeline. Beat: tenderness and the cost of silence.

chapters.title: Inspector Calloway Calls
chapters.summary: A polite inspector arrives asking about 'irregular' census entries and missing persons. Edmund lies smoothly and hates how good he's become at it. POV: Edmund. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its argument in earnest.

chapters.title: Nell on the Quay
chapters.summary: Delivering a parcel to the docks, Edmund glimpses a young woman, Nell Byrne, whose face mirrors his own. She's saving for a berth to America. POV: Edmund. Beat: vertigo—the past arriving uninvited, wearing his mother's eyes.

chapters.title: What Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Edmund searches old family papers and confirms Nell is his half-sister, the child his mother abandoned in Cork. POV: Edmund, flashback interludes. Beat: grief rewritten—he was never an only story.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Calloway offers Edmund immunity in exchange for testimony against Adeline. Edmund stalls, then burns one incriminating letter. POV: Edmund. Beat: first irreversible act; the reader feels the noose tighten.

chapters.title: Adeline's War Room
chapters.summary: Adeline reveals she's sheltering a fugitive organizer and asks Edmund, finally, to be more than a driver. POV: Adeline primarily. Beat: being trusted is heavier than being ignored.

chapters.title: Two Tickets, One Berth
chapters.summary: Edmund buys passage for Nell but learns only one berth remains on the morning tide sailing—and Calloway now watches the docks. POV: Edmund. Beat: the central dilemma crystallizes; dread becomes arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Fugitive in the Attic
chapters.summary: Calloway raids neighboring houses; the fugitive, Ruth, nearly escapes through the orchard. Edmund covers for them at personal risk. POV: Ruth briefly, then Edmund. Beat: found family forms under pressure.

chapters.title: Prowse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund confronts the census taker, discovering Prowse is blackmailing several households. A fragile alliance forms. POV: Edmund/Prowse. Beat: anger replaces fear; the hunted begin comparing notes.

chapters.title: Nell's Story
chapters.summary: Nell tells Edmund what their mother's leaving did to her—workhouses, hunger, a name given by strangers. POV: Nell. Beat: Edmund's guilt meets her forgiveness, which hurts worse than blame.

chapters.title: The Betrayal He Didn't Commit
chapters.summary: Someone informs on the Voss house; suspicion falls on Edmund because of his census irregularities. Adeline doubts him. POV: Edmund. Beat: isolation at the exact moment he needs allies most.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Orchards
chapters.summary: Edmund and Nell meet secretly among the apple trees; he offers her the berth. She refuses to take what he won't give freely. POV: alternating. Beat: love expressed as argument; the choice sharpens.

chapters.title: Ruth Is Taken
chapters.summary: Ruth is arrested; Adeline chooses public arrest over flight, becoming a martyr by design. Edmund watches his two worlds collide. POV: Edmund/Ruth. Beat: despair, and the strange clarity it brings.

chapters.title: Calloway's Bargain Renewed
chapters.summary: Calloway corners Edmund: testify, or both siblings go down. Edmund realizes the berth may be his only way to save anyone. POV: Edmund. Beat: the trap closes; every exit costs a person.

chapters.title: The Forged Manifest
chapters.summary: With Prowse's reluctant help, Edmund alters the ship's manifest so Nell can sail under a clean name—but there is room for only one. POV: Edmund. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: At the quay, Edmund puts Nell aboard and stays ashore as the whistle blows. She screams his name; he mouths goodbye. POV: Edmund, then Nell from the deck. Beat: climax of loss and love intertwined.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Edmund surrenders himself and testifies truthfully—not against Adeline, but about Prowse's blackmail and his own deceptions. POV: courtroom, Edmund's voice. Beat: truth chosen at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Adeline is acquitted on a technicality; Edmund receives a reduced sentence for cooperation. In his cell, he receives his first letter addressed to him—from Nell. POV: Edmund. Beat: bittersweet relief; identity finally owned.

chapters.title: A Regiment for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Released, Edmund returns to plant the orchard properly, joined by Adeline, Ruth, and letters from America. He is no longer invisible—he is rooted. POV: Edmund. Beat: resolution; found family gathered where history finally happened to him.
